info.title: PBB - Hub Relay Server API
info.description: API reference for the PBB Hub Relay Server. Local application endpoints use X-Relay-Key. Hub-to-hub endpoints use X-Relay-Hub-Key and may also require protocol/version or signature headers depending on relay configuration. Message audiences are declared with targets[]: each target id is a final destination HQ hub id, and systems[] lists the application systems that should consume the message at that hub. Transport next hops are computed by relay topology and are not supplied by local clients.

LaravelSessionCookie.name: laravel_session
LaravelSessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie used by the operator UI. API clients should not use this for relay integration.

CsrfHeader.name: X-CSRF-TOKEN
CsrfHeader.description: Laravel CSRF token required for browser/operator form actions that mutate state.

RelayClientKey.name: X-Relay-Key
RelayClientKey.description: Local application API key. Send the registered client token in X-Relay-Key when calling local client endpoints such as POST /api/v1/messages.

RelayHubKey.name: X-Relay-Hub-Key
RelayHubKey.description: Shared or registry-derived hub credential used for hub-to-hub relay receive/upload calls.

RelayProtocolVersion.name: X-Relay-Protocol-Version
RelayProtocolVersion.description: Optional relay protocol version header. Omit to use the server default; unsupported versions return 406 or 426.

hub_id.description: HQ numeric hub identifier for the relay that appended this hop trace entry.

event.description: Relay-side event recorded for this hop, such as submitted or received.

source_system.description: System code of the application that produced the message, for example sitrep.app.

message_type.description: Domain-qualified message type. Use a stable dotted name so handlers can match patterns such as sitrep.*.

payload_format.description: Encoding/category of payload content. Use json for normal structured messages; file/image/binary when coordinating attachment upload flows.

payload_version.description: Version of the payload contract defined by the source system.

reference_type.description: Optional source-domain reference category, such as incident, case, or assessment.

reference_id.description: Optional source-domain identifier that lets consumers correlate this relay message to an upstream record.

payload.description: Application-defined JSON payload. The relay stores and forwards this value without interpreting domain fields.

tags.description: Optional routing/search labels supplied by the sender.

priority.description: Sender priority hint used for queueing and operator visibility.

correlation_id.description: Optional id shared across related messages or retries for tracing.

attachments_count.description: Number of attachments expected for this message. Use 0 when there are none.

occurred_at.description: When the source event happened. Defaults to receive/submission time when omitted.

created_at.description: When the relay envelope was created by the sending relay. Usually supplied only in hub-to-hub calls.

content_hash.description: Optional SHA-256 hash for idempotency/audit. Relay can calculate it when omitted by local clients.

targets.description: Sender-declared final destination hubs and consuming systems. Relay computes next-hop deliveries from topology while preserving this audience.

LocalMessageSubmitRequest.description: Request body for a local application submitting a new relay message. The client declares the final audience in targets[]; relay fills origin/source hub identity and computes transport deliveries.

relay_id.description: Stable relay message id, normally a ULID. Reused across all hops for idempotency.

origin_hq_hub_id.description: HQ hub id where the message was originally submitted.

source_hub_id.description: HQ hub id of the relay sending this specific hop. This changes as the message moves upstream/downstream.

source_system.description: System code of the application that produced the message, for example sitrep.app.

target_hq_hub_id.description: Immediate next-hop HQ hub id for this transport request. This is not the full audience; see targets[].

hop_trace.description: Ordered list of relay hops already visited. Receivers append themselves and reject loops.

message_type.description: Domain-qualified message type. Use a stable dotted name so handlers can match patterns such as sitrep.*.

payload_format.description: Encoding/category of payload content. Use json for normal structured messages; file/image/binary when coordinating attachment upload flows.

payload_version.description: Version of the payload contract defined by the source system.

reference_type.description: Optional source-domain reference category, such as incident, case, or assessment.

reference_id.description: Optional source-domain identifier that lets consumers correlate this relay message to an upstream record.

payload.description: Application-defined JSON payload. The relay stores and forwards this value without interpreting domain fields.

tags.description: Optional routing/search labels supplied by the sender.

priority.description: Sender priority hint used for queueing and operator visibility.

correlation_id.description: Optional id shared across related messages or retries for tracing.

attachments_count.description: Number of attachments expected for this message. Use 0 when there are none.

occurred_at.description: When the source event happened. Defaults to receive/submission time when omitted.

created_at.description: When the relay envelope was created by the sending relay. Usually supplied only in hub-to-hub calls.

content_hash.description: Optional SHA-256 hash for idempotency/audit. Relay can calculate it when omitted by local clients.

targets.description: Sender-declared final destination hubs and consuming systems preserved across hops.

RelayHopEnvelope.description: Hub-to-hub transport envelope. target_hq_hub_id names this immediate receive hop; targets[] preserves the final sender-declared audience.

total.description: Total records matching the request as reported by this endpoint.

success.description: True when the relay accepted or idempotently recognized the message.

status.description: Receive outcome. duplicate means relay_id was already recorded; undeliverable means no local client matched and no forwarding path remained.

relay_id.description: Relay id from the accepted envelope.

id.description: Final destination HQ hub id. Intermediate relays forward toward this id even when they are not a target.

systems.description: Application system codes that should consume the message when it reaches this target hub. A relay only dispatches to local handlers for systems listed under its own target id.

MessageTarget.description: One final audience entry declared by the sender. id identifies the destination hub; systems identifies consuming applications at that hub.

post.summary: Submit a relay message
post.description: Creates an outbound relay message owned by the authenticated local client. The client declares final destination hubs and consuming systems in targets[]. Relay reads the local hub id from /hub.json, injects origin/source hub identity, and computes first-hop deliveries from topology.

post.description: Accepts one inbound hop envelope from another relay. The receiving relay validates that target_hq_hub_id is the local hub, appends hop_trace, dispatches to local handlers only when targets[] contains the local hub id, and forwards to remaining target hubs when topology allows.
